articles.title: Jeshaun Jones Suspended for First Three Games of Regular Season
articles.summary: Not great timing for a fringe player
articles.body:
A member of the Minnesota Vikings who is currently fighting for a spot on the 53-man roster has just seen his chances of not being a part of the team's final cuts increase dramatically. . .for the wrong reasons.

The National Football League has informed Vikings' wide receiver Jeshaun Jones that he will be suspended for the first three games of the 2026 regular season for violating the league's substance abuse policy. He can continue participating in the team's preseason program, including Friday's game in Denver against the Broncos, before starting his suspension on 30 August.

Jones was reportedly arrested outside of Tampa on 18 April for refusing to submit to a blood test to determine his blood-alcohol level. He pleaded guilty to a lesser charge of reckless driving last month, with a sentence that includes twelve months of probation.

While Jones' chances of making the active roster appear to be slim, he would not count against the 53-man roster during the time he is on the suspended list if the Vikings wanted to keep him around. Jones, who leads the Vikings in receiving yardage through the first two preseason games, has been on the team's practice squad the past two seasons and would likely be a candidate to be there again this season.

Jones will be eligible to return at the start of Week 4, so we will see if this incident plays any role in whether or not the team brings him back or decides to cut ties with him completely.

articles.title: Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad: How to Watch Today as Madrid’s Injury Problems Grow

articles.body:
Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad takes place at the Santiago Bernabéu on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, in the rearranged La Liga Matchday 1 fixture. Kick-off is set for 9:00 p.m. CEST, or 8:00 p.m. BST. Real Madrid will play their first home league game of the season after opening the campaign with a 2-1 win away to Espanyol.

Real Sociedad, meanwhile, arrive in Madrid after losing 1-0 to Real Betis . The fixture was moved from its original date because several Real Madrid players were still involved in the 2026 World Cup.

José Mourinho will lead Real Madrid into his first competitive home match since returning to the club. Pellegrino Matarazzo will take charge of Real Sociedad as both teams look to improve their early league position.

Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad will see Mourinho manage a squad affected by early injuries. Éder Militão and Rodrygo are unavailable, while Ferland Mendy , Raúl Asencio and Thiago Pitarch are also sidelined according to the match information supplied. Real Madrid started the season with a 2-1 win at Espanyol, with new signing Carlos Espí scoring the 90th-minute winner. Jude Bellingham had earlier put Madrid ahead before Espanyol equalized.

Real Sociedad began with a 1-0 defeat against Real Betis. Mikel Oyarzabal is among the key players available to Matarazzo, while Álvaro Odriozola remains out with a long-term knee injury. Gonçalo Guedes and Pablo Marín faced fitness checks before the match.

Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad Lineups and Key Numbers

The confirmed Real Madrid lineup includes Thibaut Courtois , Denzel Dumfries , Álvaro Carreras, Federico Valverde , Ibrahima Konaté, Dean Huijsen , Arda Güler, Bernardo Silva , Kylian Mbappé , Jude Bellingham and Vinícius Júnior . Mourinho has selected a 4-2-3-1 formation.

Real Sociedad's starting team includes Álex Remiro , Jon Aramburu , Sergio Gómez , Carlos Soler , Igor Zubeldia , Jon Martín, Takefusa Kubo , Yangel Herrera , Orri Steinn Óskarsson and Luka Sučić, with the final attacking position listed for Gonçalo Guedes in the confirmed lineup. Matarazzo also uses a 4-2-3-1 shape. Oyarzabal is among the substitutes.

Real Madrid have won four of their last five meetings with Real Sociedad. Their most recent meeting at the Bernabéu ended in a 4-1 Real Madrid victory in February 2026, with Vinícius Júnior scoring twice. The teams also played out a 4-4 Copa del Rey draw in April 2025.

Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad: How to Watch and Match Details

Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad kicks off at 9:00 p.m. CEST at the Santiago Bernabéu. Real Madrid's official schedule confirms the match was postponed from Matchday 1 because of World Cup commitments.

In Spain , the match is listed on Orange TV and Movistar LaLiga. Viewers outside Spain can also follow the match through regional broadcasters. Fans in the UK can use Premier Sports or LaLigaTV, while DAZN has coverage in Italy and Germany .

In the US, ESPN+ and ESPN Deportes will carry La Liga, with TSN+ serving viewers in Canada . beIN Sports covers the Middle East and North Africa, while SuperSport provides La Liga coverage across Sub-Saharan Africa.

articles.title: O'Neill takes responsibility with nowhere to hide for Celtic
articles.summary: Celtic manager Martin O'Neill says his team have a "million miles to go" after defeat in Austria.
articles.body:
In the open air of the Raiffeisen Arena, with bedlam all around, there was nowhere to hide for Celtic or Martin O'Neill.

The Scottish champions had endured one of the darkest nights in their European history.

After going out to Kairat Almaty on penalties last year at this stage of the Champions League play-offs, that is saying something.

Four goals up on aggregate against LASK, O'Neill's Celtic somehow conspired to implode in a second half with little sign of a response on the way to a 5-4 aggregate loss following extra time.

There was no hiding place, and the Celtic manager was frank when put in the spotlight at full-time.

"I'm responsible for this one," he said.

"Without a doubt. Naturally it took me a long time to get over the Uefa Cup final in 2003 but this was majorly disappointing.

"In the context of things, one was a final which it would have been terrific to win, this was a qualifying game which we should have been able to get through.

"We know that we are a million miles from the finished article. That's absolutely true. I think we thought that anyway."

Celtic blow four-goal lead to LASK in Champions League collapse

Exhausted & fragile - how Celtic's capitulation unfolded

O'Neill was not in charge for that defeat in Kazakhstan a year ago as it triggered the start of the end for Brendan Rodgers' second spell at Celtic Park.

The current Parkhead boss helped steady Celtic's ship last term following Rodgers' exit and again following the Wilfried Nancy saga to guide them to another league title and a Scottish Cup.

This season appeared to get off to a prosperous start until the roof began to cave in over in Austria .

Away from the raw pain of stumbling in such a stark way, the aftermath could be telling for Celtic who now have to not only pick themselves up, but finish off a transfer window without the hefty windfall which would have blown in with the Champions League.

"The qualification for the Champions League is major, it's major in every aspect," said O'Neill.

"Financially, for prestige, but we have to pick ourselves up. That's my responsibility again to do that.

"I think I said last week that if you could qualify for the Champions League there would be players wanting to come on that basis.

"That's not going to be the case but we'll see. Tonight we came up well and truly short, particularly in the second half."

Celtic captain Callum McGregor tells Amazon Prime: "We got what we deserved. We were passive all night. We looked scared to go and win the game.

"I didn't think we were that good in the first leg either. We scored at good times and got away with it.

"We have to suck it up. We apologise to our supporters and the club because there's no way we should lose that game.

"It's as much on the players as everyone else. You can't look for excuses elsewhere.

"You'll now see what people are made of. When you play like that you can't have any excuses whatsoever.

"When you go 1-0 up in the game and it still doesn't settle you, you can't have any excuse and that's on us.

"You fall at a big hurdle and these questions [on whether the squad are ready] are going to be asked. You can't lose by that margin then look for excuses elsewhere.

"This is what it's like to play at Celtic. You have to bounce back, you have to show a reaction and that's what Celtic are all about."

Former Celtic captain Scott Brown on BBC Radio Scotland: " It was a fantastic start, you go 1-0 up, but that seems like forever ago. Now they've crashed out the Champions League and conceded five goals.

"LASK outran Celtic in a couple of areas, the two up front were strong, solid and willing runners.

"LASK deserve to go through with that performance. I feel for the lads because I've been in that situation as well."

Former Celtic manager Neil Lennon on Amazon Prime: "It looked to me as if Celtic were exhausted. Fragile in duels. It only looked like there would be one winner.

"They battered Celtic tonight, physically and on the football side. It could have been more."

Former Celtic midfielder Stiliyan Petrov: "Everyone [is to blame].

"They are all in it together. A big club like Celtic should be able to hold that out."

articles.title: Bruno Fernandes and Khadija Shaw win PFA Player of the Year awards
articles.summary: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has been crowned Professional Footballers' Association Player of the Year as Manchester City's Khadija Shaw won the...
articles.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has been crowned Professional Footballers' Association Player of the Year as Manchester City 's Khadija Shaw won the women's award for the second time.

Playmaker Fernandes broke the all-time record for Premier League assists during an outstanding 2025-26 campaign, setting up 21 goals as he surpassed Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne .

The 31-year-old also scored nine times as United overcome a shaky first half of the campaign to finish third in the Premier League under Michael Carrick and earn a Champions League return.

Fernandes was pleased to have been voted the winner by his fellow professionals.

He said: "It is obviously a very proud moment. They are the ones you go on the pitch against and it's probably not easy to vote for someone you play against, so it is a very good moment."

The Portugal international is the Red Devils' first winner since Wayne Rooney took home the trophy in 2009-10 and adds to his Football Writers' Association Footballer of the Year award from May.

Manchester City sharpshooter Shaw, who was also recognized by the FWA, scooped the PFA Women's Player of the Year award for the second time.

The 29-year-old claimed the trophy in 2023-24 and won it again having scored 21 goals on the way to a third straight Golden Boot and her maiden Women's Super League title.

Arsenal 's Olivia Smith picked up the women's PFA Young Player of the Year title for the second campaign running, having won the 2025 crown for her exploits at Liverpool and continued her form in the capital.

Manchester City's Nico O'Reilly was named men's PFA Young Player of the Year following an outstanding campaign that ended with the versatile talent helping England to win World Cup bronze.

The 21-year-old was part of the PFA Premier League Team of the Year along with City team-mates Erling Haaland , Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo .

O'Reilly said: "I had a great season. I'm very proud of the season I had. I won two trophies with my club and managed to play at the World Cup with my country. I'm over the moon how it turned out."

Champions Arsenal had five representatives in David Raya , Gabriel, William Saliba , Jurrien Timber and Declan Rice , with Player of the Year Fernandes of United and Brentford 's Igor Thiago completing the team.

The PFA WSL Team of the Year featured three players from triumphant City, with Shaw joined by team-mates Kerstin Casparij and Yui Hasegawa .

Mariona Caldentey , last year's PFA Women's Player of the Year, was joined in the XI by fellow Arsenal players Emily Fox and Alessia Russo .

Tottenham defender Toko Koga and Manchester United's Jess Park were also included in a team, as were the Chelsea trio of Hannah Hampton , Ellie Carpenter and Lauren James .

Kenny Dalglish and Karen Carney received the PFA merit awards in recognition of their contribution to football.

Dalglish enjoyed a success-laden career as player with Celtic and Liverpool, and is Scotland 's most capped player having represented his country on 102 occasions.

The 75-year-old, who confirmed in June he was undergoing treatment for cancer, went on to enjoy a successful managerial career, leading Liverpool to three league titles before masterminding Blackburn's Premier League triumph.

Carney played 144 times for England, including being part of the Lionesses squad which finished third at the 2015 World Cup.

Having come through the ranks at Birmingham, Carney won the quadruple with Arsenal in 2007 as well as a league and FA Cup double with Chelsea in 2018.

articles.title: Football safety remains focus as new CTE study released
articles.summary: As football season kicks off for Durham Public Schools, athletic leaders are taking steps to keep student-athletes safer.
articles.body:
As football season gets underway for Durham Public Schools, safety remains a top concern as researchers continue to learn more about chronic traumatic encephalopathy, or CTE.

CTE is a brain disease linked to repeated head impacts.

"It's a progressive neurodegenerative condition that comes from sustaining repeated blows to the head over time," neurologist Leah Croll said.

A new study found that at least 25% of NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 had CTE. Croll said head impacts do not have to result in a concussion to increase the risk of developing the disease.

"They can be what we call sub-concussive hits," Croll said. "Over time, having more and more instances where you're hit in the head, that can contribute to increasing your risk for developing this condition."

Advocates described the study as a "sobering reminder that football carries real risks."

In a statement to ABC11, the NFL said the league "continuously strives to make the game of football safer, including by implementing strategies to reduce concussions and head impacts."

CTE can only be diagnosed after death, meaning research has relied heavily on brains donated by players and their families. Researchers say that limitation makes it difficult to fully understand how the disease develops and how it can be prevented or treated in living people.

"It really slows down our research efforts when it comes to prevention and treatment of CTE, and that's a huge problem, particularly when it comes to kids," Croll said.

The study comes as a 17-year-old high school quarterback in Wisconsin died after suffering an on-field injury during a game.

"Any time a student-athlete loses their life or suffers a severe head trauma is concerning to everyone," Durham Public Schools athletic director David Hackney said. "We try to take every safety measure to try to prevent those things from happening."

Durham Public Schools uses Guardian Caps, soft-shell padding worn over traditional football helmets. Hackney said the equipment has helped student-athletes.

"I think Guardian Caps is a big step, but we can take it a step further," Hackney said.

Hackney said licensed professionals are also on-site at Durham football games to evaluate injuries. After an injury, an athletic trainer assesses when it is safe for a student-athlete to return to action.

"We monitor concussion protocols," Hackney said. "Our athletic trainers do an awesome job of making sure they're following up with the student-athlete, as well as their parents, to make sure that they're following all those safety measures and that they take every precaution before they are allowed back on the field."

School officials said those measures are intended to reduce risks and help protect student-athletes throughout the football season.

articles.title: Lucas Ocampos, líder de goleo en Liga MX, falla penalti ante Chicago en Leagues Cup
articles.standfirst: El delantero no pudo darle la ventaja a Rayados en los Cuartos de Final
articles.summary: El delantero no pudo darle la ventaja a Rayados en los Cuartos de Final
articles.body: Lucas Ocampos es uno de los mejores futbolistas de los Rayados por lo que durante el partido de Cuartos de Final de la Leagues Cup ante Chicago Fire le dieron la responsabilidad de tirar un penal para así tomar ventaja en el duelo, pero lamentablemente falló, siendo el primero que no puede mandar a las redes con la playera de Monterrey Y es que durante los últimos partidos de Monterrey había sido el jugador clave para el esquema de Matías Almeyda, siendo el líder de la tabla de goleo del Apertura 2026 con cinco tantos, pero que ahora no pudo ser determinante para sus Rayados que deberán seguir remando contra el público local que juega su partido y explotó con la falla de la pena máxima. Corría el minuto 40' del primer tiempo cuando un pase filtrado rompió la defensa de los estadounidenses y un puñetazo en la cara del atacante de Monterrey terminó por marcarse como penal por lo que rápidamente la responsabilidad pasó a Lucas Ocampos, el goleador de Rayados. Sin embargo, tomó el balón y cuando disparó logró engañar al portero Brady de Chicago, pero fue tanta la potencia que terminó por estrellarse el el palo para así ahogar el grito de gol de La Pandilla y Matías Almeyda, quien animo rápidamente a su delantero que solo comenzó a sonreir. Lucas Ocampos está viviendo un segundo aire con Rayados y se ha convertido en uno de los principales referentes ofensivos del equipo. El argentino suma cinco goles en cinco jornadas del Apertura 2026, cifra que lo coloca como líder momentáneo de goleo y que ya iguala los tantos que consiguió durante todo el Apertura 2025. Bajo el mando de Matías Almeyda, recuperó protagonismo, confianza y libertad para aparecer desde distintas zonas del campo. El rendimiento del argentino es todavía más llamativo porque no es un centro delantero natural. Desde su llegada a Monterrey suma 15 goles en 74 partidos, pero ahora atraviesa su mejor momento goleador con Rayados y es pieza clave de la ofensiva más productiva del torneo, con 12 anotaciones en cuatro jornadas. articles.title: Pumas se pudo quedar sin el Chino Huerta por culpa de un club de España
articles.standfirst: Se dio a conocer hace poco que un club de España pudo haber fichado a Cesar Huerta, pero el jugador se decidió por otro rumbo
articles.summary: Se dio a conocer hace poco que un club de España pudo haber fichado a Cesar Huerta, pero el jugador se decidió por otro rumbo
articles.body: El Chino Huerta volverá a la Liga MX tras estar durante año y medio en el Anderlecht, el cual se encuentra en la Primera División de Bélgica donde tuvo un inicio llamativo, pero no consiguió destacar durante su estancia en el club Belga por lo que muchos equipos mexicanos buscaron repatriar al jugador mexicano, pero al final decidió regresar a los Pumas. Por otro lado, hace poco salió a la luz que no solo el Club Belga estaba interesado por él, si no que un club de la Liga Española también estaba interesado, además había igualado el sueldo que le ofreció el Anderlecht. En diciembre de 2024, le llegó información a FOX Sports de que Pumas sostuvo negociaciones con el Anderlecht y Osasuna para fichar al Chino Huerta, el cual terminó fichando por el conjunto Belga. Hace unos días Raúl Ortiz reveló un dato que cambia por completo esta historia, durante el programa llamado La Última Palabra reveló que el extremo mexicano tuvo la oportunidad de hacer su traspaso hacia el Osasuna por el mismo sueldo que el Anderlecht. Siendo una decisión muy criticada, al tener una mejor oportunidad deportiva, teniendo la facilidad de llegar a una de las 5 grandes ligas del futbol Europeo, pero al final decidió ir por una liga de menor nivel. De acuerdo con información de Rodrigo Tovar, reveló que Chino Huerta llegará esta semana a la Ciudad de México para reportar con Pumas y firmar el contrato que lo vincule nuevamente con el Club Universidad Nacional para iniciar su segunda etapa. El jugador mexicano llega con los siguientes números de su antiguo club, el Anderlecht: No solo los Auriazules estaba interesado en los servicios de Cesar Huerta, se mencionaba que clubes como América, Monterrey, Cruz Azul y Toluca también se interesaron en el extremo de 25 años, quien le dio prioridad a Pumas. Siendo un club muy importante dentro de su carrera, llegando en el Apertura 2022, después de haber pasado por Chivas, Zacatepec, Monarcas Morelia, Tapatío y más recientemente, por el extinto Mazatlán FC. Llegó como un futbolista aún en etapa de adaptación, aunque fue contando con un crecimiento progresivo, hasta que se fue convirtiendo en un jugador cada vez más importante para el ataque universitario. Su mejor torneo fue el Apertura 2023, mismo en donde marcó 8 goles y ayudó a Pumas a llegar hasta las semifinales, siendo el momento donde se consolidó como uno de los principales referentes ofensivos del equipo. articles.title: El clásico regio entre Tigres y Rayados cambia de fecha, anuncia la Liga MX
articles.standfirst: Ese partido marcará el regreso de Víctor Manuel Vucetich al Gigante de Acero
articles.summary: Ese partido marcará el regreso de Víctor Manuel Vucetich al Gigante de Acero
articles.body: La próxima edición del Clásico Regio entre Monterrey y Tigres, correspondiente a la Jornada 8 del Apertura 2026, tendrá una modificación, la información la dio a conocer este día la Liga MX, mediante un comunicado, este duelo ha generado mucha expectativa pues será el primero de Víctor Manuel Vucetich ante Rayados luego de dos etapas con la Pandilla y además, será su regreso al ‘Gigante de Acero’, solo que con el rival de toda la vida. El Clásico Regio es sin duda uno de los partidos más atractivos de la fase regular de cada torneo en la Liga MX, Rayados y Tigres dividen la ciudad y el duelo empieza a palpitarse con un ambiente especial luego de la llegada de Vucetich con los Felinos, equipo al que ya había dirigido pero estaba más identificado con Monterrey, con el que además logró varios títulos. Mediante un comunicado que compartió en sus redes sociales, la Liga MX dio a conocer que la próxima edición del Clásico Regio entre Rayados y Tigres que originalmente estaba pactada para el domingo 13 de septiembre, cambia de día para el sábado 12 de septiembre en punto de las 19 horas. Aunque de entrada se comenzó a especular con los motivos del cambio de día, la Liga MX no dio detalles sobre la modificación del próximo Clásico Regio, en el que la afición de Monterrey se encontrará con el histórico director técnico de La Pandilla y a quien le deben varias estrellas en el escudo El Clásico Regio también tendrá el ingrediente de que será el primero para Matías Almeyda y además, será la primera vez que el ‘Pelado’ se enfrente a Víctor Manuel Vucetich desde enero de 2017 cuando Chivas venció a Querétaro 1-0, un entrenador ante el que nunca perdió en su anterior etapa en la Liga MX, sumando 3 victorias y 2 empates.

articles.summary: La gran rivalidad se dará en Oakland en la primera Fecha FIFA del semestre
articles.body: La máxima rivalidad a nivel de clubes en la Liga MX es sin duda el llamado Clásico Nacional entre las Águilas del América y las Chivas Rayadas del Guadalajara año con años tenemos, al menos dos juegos oficiales entre ambas instituciones, normalmente uno de ellos se da en el primer semestre del año en el torneo Clausura y el segundo en el torneo Apertura, también lo más común es que uno de ellos será en el Estadio Banorte de la Ciudad de México y el otro en el Estadio Akron de Zapopan, Jalisco; sin embargo, nunca nos quedamos con esos dos duelos y ahora conocemos al menos uno más en este 2026. Y es que se ha dado a conocer un duelo amistoso entre los de Coapa y los de Verde Valle, como no es nada nuevo, en Estados Unidos, en donde seguramente habrá un lleno monumental y un ingreso en taquilla descomunal por lo que mueven ambas instituciones en el vecino del norte, además servirá para mantener a los equipos que dirigen el uruguayo Guillermo Almada y el argentino Gabriel Milito a tope para seguir encarando de gran manera el torneo Apertura 2026 de la Liga MX. El duelo se llevará al cabo durante la siguiente Fecha FIFA que será la primera tras la conclusión de la Copa Mundial de la FIFA 2026, que se desarrollará entre el 21 de septiembre y el 6 de octubre del presente año, el duelo se escenificará el domingo 4 de octubre en el Oakland Alameda County Coliseum a las 7:00 pm (hora del centro de México) en aquella ciudad de la bahía californiana, antigua casa de los entonces Oakland Raiders de la NFL y los Oakland Athletics de la MLB, ambas franquicias ahora ubicadas en otros mercados.

articles.title: Resumen y goles Rayados vs Chicago Fire: Cañonazo de Orbelín Pineda manda a Matías Almeyda a semifinales de Leagues Cup
articles.standfirst: La Pandilla espera rival en semifinales
articles.summary: La Pandilla espera rival en semifinales
articles.body: Arrancaron los cuartos de final de la Leagues Cup y Monterrey es el primer equipo de la Liga MX clasificar a semifinales del torneo gracias a un golazo de Orbelín Pineda cuando parecía que el partido ante Chicago Fire se definía en la tanda de penales y también gracias a la gran actuación de Esteban Andrada en la primera mitad. Almeyda y Monterrey ahora esperan rival y con esto se confirma lo que el entrenador argentino sobre el interés que tienen en quedarse con la Leagues Cup y ahora están solo a un partido de llegar a la Gran Final que por cierto, se disputará en septiembre y de paso, ser el primer equipo de la Liga MX en ganar el certamen desde que lo hizo León en el 2021. El primer tiempo comenzó con mucha dinámica, en general los 45 minutos iniciales fueron muy entretenidos y tuvieron varios protagonistas, uno de ellos Esteban Andrada que regresó a la titularidad con Monterrey y tuvo un par de atajadas con las que mantuvo su portería en cero y desde luego mostró que está para pelear por el puesto no solo en la Leagues Cup, sino en el Apertura 2026. Monterrey de a poco comenzó a generar peligro y la primera oportunidad clara que tuvo para adelantarse fue un penal que cobró el árbitro y que pudo costarle la tarjeta roja al arquero de Chicago Fire, Chris Brady, solo que cuando el árbitro revisó el VAR pues había un puñetazo claro sobre Hugo Cuypers, decidió mantener la tarjeta amarilla. Antes de finalizar el primer tiempo, llegó el primer gol de Monterrey tras un centro que llegó desde la banda izquierda y que remató de cabeza Víctor Guzmán, que no hacía un gol desde hace un año, una anotación sin duda, muy importante para él y también para La Pandilla. La segunda mitad tuvo a Chicago Fire como el dueño de la pelota y en un error de Lucas Ocampos, Gutman no lo pensó dos veces para meter un centro que remató de zurda Philip Zinkernagel para el 1-1 cuando ya se jugaban los últimos 30 minutos del partido y aunque todo indicaba que el partido se iba a definir en penales, apareció Orbelín Pineda con un golazo para sellar el pase a semifinales para Monterrey

articles.title: Chicago Fire eliminated by Monterrey in Leagues Cup quarterfinal
articles.summary: By Jaime UribarriChicago Fire FC were eliminated from Leagues Cup 2026 in the quarterfinals on Tuesday night, falling 2-1 to CF Monterrey at SeatGeek Stadium...
articles.body:
Chicago Fire FC were eliminated from Leagues Cup 2026 in the quarterfinals on Tuesday night, falling 2-1 to CF Monterrey at SeatGeek Stadium.

Orbelín Pineda 's stunning 83rd-minute strike tilted the balance in favor of the LIGA MX outfit, who will face either the Columbus Crew or Club América next week in the semifinals.

Monterrey took the lead at the stroke of halftime via Víctor Guzmán's close-range header. Rayados could've opened the score earlier after Chicago goalkeeper Chris Brady fouled ex-Fire striker Hugo Cuypers inside the box, but Lucas Ocampos smashed his penalty kick off the post.

Philip Zinckernagel' s 59th-minute leveller provided a spark for Chicago, only for Pineda to bury their hopes and secure passage for Monterrey with a world-class volley.

articles.title: Scott Ponder looks to lead Alto back to the playoffs for the first time since 2021

articles.body:
ALTO, Texas ( KETK ) – Alto head football coach Scott Ponder hasn't had to do much motivating since he arrived on campus earlier this year.

Alto football riding three-game win streak as Yellowjackets eye first playoff trip since 2021

"We wanna win. We wanna be a good team. I mean, we got a ways to go but the 'want to' is there. And that's the number one thing you gotta have," Ponder said.

The Yellowjackets haven't made the playoffs since 2021 and are more than ready to end that streak.

"Not making the playoffs sucks but I think we're predicted to win district this year. You know, just not being an underdog and everybody believing in us it just feels really good," senior quarterback Camdyn Almond said.

"Last year we definitely should've made the playoffs but we came up short. The year before that, it was the same thing, so this year I'm definitely planning on hitting the playoffs and making a run there. Just not making it but making a run as well," senior running back and safety AJ Buckingham said.

After four seasons at Mount Enterprise, where Ponder led the Wildcats to the playoffs three times including a state semifinal appearance in 2025, he took over at district foe Alto back in January.

"Feel like he's just brought everybody's confidence back cuz everybody rallies around Coach Ponder. Everybody loves that guy so everybody's willing to go to war for him, and it's just made everybody play better," Almond said.

Ponder said it was a tough decision to leave Mount Enterprise but he's excited to be in Alto and can't wait to lead the Yellowjackets into battle.

"Alto's a football town. It's important to the community. They got flags hanging on every pole in town. And they wanna win. They wanna be successful and that's intriguing and exciting, and the kids buy into that and that history. We gotta put a product on the field that matches that enthusiasm of the community," Ponder said.

Almond said Alto's experience will make them tough to beat this fall.

"Our senior class is pretty big. A lot of those guys started as freshmen and just started every year since then," Almond said.

Buckingham senses a belief growing within the Yellowjackets program and in the Alto community.

"Not only do we believe but the community believes again as well and that's exciting," Buckingham said.

Ponder and the Yellowjackets open the season on the road at Groveton on Friday, August 28.

Kickoff is set for 7:30 p.m. at John W. Reynolds Athletic Complex in Groveton.

articles.title: High quality, low risk: record number of Japanese in Premier League
articles.summary: A record number of Japanese players are in the Premier League this season, with clubs attracted by their proven quality, value for money and the "very little...
articles.body:
A record number of Japan ese players are in the Premier League this season, with clubs attracted by their proven quality, value for money and the "very little risk" involved in signing them.

Ten players from Japan were registered with top-tier English teams when the campaign kicked off last weekend and more are potentially on the way before the transfer window closes.

Zion Suzuki was the highest-profile arrival with his switch to Aston Villa , with former Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu returning to London with Crystal Palace , midfielder Hidemasa Morita joining Hull City and Daizen Maeda swapping Celtic for Ipswich Town.

They join an established group of Japanese players already in the Premier League, including Brighton 's Kaoru Mitoma , Liverpool 's Wataru Endo and Palace's Daichi Kamada .

FIFA-registered agent Joel Pannick of CAA Base told AFP that English clubs have "increased confidence that signing a Japanese player is a good move to make".

"There aren't many examples of clubs signing Japanese players and having issues with their adaptation, with their personality, with their integration into the squad, with discipline," said Pannick, who has about 60 Japanese players on his books.

"The risk element that teams previously feared, this fear of the unknown, has gone because with each example of a successful Japanese player it gives more confidence," he added.

Also in the Premier League are Ao Tanaka ( Leeds ), Kota Takai ( Spurs ) and Tatsuhiro Sakamoto (Coventry).

Midfielder Tanaka, who has played 41 times for Japan, joined from German side Fortuna Dusseldorf for just £3.3 million (now $4.5 million) two years ago.

Japanese players in England have come a long way since Junichi Inamoto signed for Arsenal in 2001 and left for Fulham a year later without making a league appearance.

There have been successes along the way, with Shinji Kagawa , Shinji Okazaki , Takumi Minamino and Endo all picking up league winner's medals.

Suzuki, 24, will become the first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Premier League if he makes his debut after joining Villa from Italian side Parma last week.

Veteran Japanese football journalist Yoshiyuki Osumi says he is "10 or 20 years ahead of his time for a Japanese goalkeeper".

"If he can play in the Premier League as a goalkeeper, I think that would have a big impact on Japanese football," said Osumi.

Suzuki's transition to the Premier League will be helped by the fact that he can already communicate in English.

Not all of his compatriots have had that ability in the past, but more are realising that being able to speak the language is crucial to succeeding in Europe.

Pannick says that his client Maya Yoshida started a culture change when he captained the Japan national team ahead of the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

Pannick says that Yoshida, who spent almost eight years at Southampton, would insist that any player who sat at his lunch table must communicate in English.

"To get this more worldly mentality is something that he was very keen to emphasise to the players," said Pannick.

"This current generation of starting national team players or squad players at the World Cup, almost all of them now will speak English to a pretty good degree."

Most Japanese players will spend time in other European leagues like Belgium , the Netherlands or Portugal before making the step up to the Premier League.

The Championship has become another popular staging post, and there are currently eight Japanese players in England's second tier.

Post-Brexit changes to work permit rules have forced English clubs to look beyond Europe for signings.

Journalist Osumi says an overall improvement in the level of Japanese players has allowed them to thrive in the Premier League.

But he believes a change in the nature of the league has also made it easier for them to adapt.

"The Premier League has become more tactical, and there are more teams that play as a coordinated unit," he said.

"That kind of football is something Japanese players find very easy to adapt to."

articles.title: La EFC alcanza los 850 clubes europeos con el 'fichaje' del Racing de Santander
articles.standfirst: La Asociación de clubes europeos hace historia en un año clave para la gobernanza del fútbol
articles.summary: La Asociación de clubes europeos marca un nuevo récord en un año clave para
articles.body: La Asociación de clubes europeos (EFC) sigue creciendo y ha anunciado que cuenta ya con 850 clubes afiliados. "La reciente incorporación del Real Racing Club (España), tras las del KS Kastrioti (Albania), el FC Groningen (Países Bajos), el FC Kolkheti Khobi (Georgia) y el Hull City AFC (Inglaterra), supone otro hito simbólico en la misión de EFC de situar a los clubes y sus intereses en el centro del fútbol", apunta la organización en un comunicado. Para la EFC es importante seguir creciendo en un año muy importante en la gobernanza del fútbol y donde van a jugar un papel clave como el único interlocutor válido en representación de los 55 países europeos para la UEFA y FIFA, que a lo largo de esta temporada celebran elecciones para su presidencia, con Gianni Infantino en un momento complicado y con el posible relevo para Aleksander Ceferin. "Esta cifra histórica también subraya la capacidad de la EFC para reunir a clubes de todos los tamaños y perfiles de 55 países y territorios. La EFC, reconocida por la UEFA y la FIFA como el único organismo representativo de los clubes de fútbol en Europa, garantiza que los intereses de todos sus miembros estén plenamente representados en los debates y decisiones que dan forma al futuro del fútbol de clubes europeo e internacional", añade el comunicado. De la mano de Nasser al Khelaifi, la EFC, que este mes de septiembre va a celebrar en Copenhague su Asamblea General, no ha dejado de crecer, jugando un papel esencial contra la Superliga que ahora ya es historia. "Alcanzar los 850 miembros es otro hito fantástico para la EFC y refleja nuestra misión continua de representar y brindar importantes beneficios y servicios a clubes de todos los tamaños y tipos en toda Europa. Nos enorgullece que EFC trabaje de forma positiva y en estrecha colaboración con todas las partes interesadas, garantizando que nuestros miembros tengan voz en las decisiones que dan forma al futuro del fútbol de clubes europeo e internacional y construyendo colectivamente un ecosistema mejor para todos", comenta el presidente.

articles.title: "Me recuerda al descaro y la cara que tenía Jesé"
articles.standfirst: Con 16 años, Rafa Cruz se ha convertido en la última perla de la cantera canaria
articles.summary: Con 16 años, Rafa Cruz se ha convertido en la última perla de la cantera canaria
articles.body: Rafa Cruz se convirtió hace unos días en el tercer jugador más joven en debutar con la UD Las Palmas. Cuando pisó el césped del Gran Canaria, la afición lo recibió como un regalo adelantado a un triunfo (contra el Albacete) que se consiguió en el minuto 93. La historia de Rafa Cruz es la de última perla de la cantera canaria: "Estoy muy orgullosa, pero también siento un poco de vértigo e incertidumbre, porque es un niño todavía. Creo que mi hijo todavía ni se cree lo que está viviendo". Son las palabras de la orgullosa madre, Mariola. Ella, como el resto de su familia, tuvo problemas para conciliar el sueño tras ver a su hijo debutar: "Es una sensación que no puedo explicar con palabras, sólo dar las gracias. Yo tengo que agradecer a la afición como acogieron al chiquillo. Todavía recuerdo cuando nombraron su nombre y me da sentimiento", admite todavía emocionada. Su debut se ha ido cocinando a fuego lento. Ya el pasado curso fue convocado por Luis García para viajar a Cádiz y, aunque saltó a calentar, no tuvo minutos. Pero desde ese momento se le comunicó que pasaría a ser, con apenas 16 años, parte del primer equipo. Rubén de la Barrera le dio la alternativa ante el Albacete en la primera jornada de Liga: "Estoy contento con el debut de Rafa. Queremos ayudarle para que tenga la tranquilidad necesaria y pueda ir dando los pasos adecuados", admitió el gallego. Un debut con el que Rafa lleva soñando desde benjamines, cuando jugaba en la escuela de fútbol del Veteranos del Pilar junto a su hermano Jorge: "Desde el primer día empezaron a despuntar y lo pasaron a jugar con los mayores", explica Mariola. Fue cuando Rafa Cruz se cruzó por primera vez con Sixto Alfonso, ojeador del Real Madrid: "Era un chico diferente. Lo que vemos ahora es lo mismo que vimos cuando era infantil. Se caracteriza por ser un jugador de los que encara y no le importa intentarlo una y otra vez, porque se puede ir por fuera y por dentro. Me recuerda al descaro y la cara que tenía Jesé. Es cierto que en el debut lo vi algo nervioso, pero es normal... tiene 16 años", sentencia. No tardó la UD en fijarse en él, ya que en segundo año de benjamines ya era amarillo. Pero la figura de Sixto nunca se separó del camino de Rafa Cruz. Él se encargó llevarlo al Real Madrid en categoría cadete: "Estuvo la primera temporada, pero al poco de comenzar la segunda se volvió. Futbolísticamente no tuvo problema alguno, todo lo contrario, pero sí es cierto que no se acabó de adaptar a vivir lejos de su familia, y más concretamente de su hermano", algo con lo que está de acuerdo su madre: "Ellos tienen un vínculo muy especial. Ya por octubre lo veía raro, sentía como madre que no estaba bien. Hasta que me mandó un mensaje diciéndome, con mucho sentimiento, que se quería volver a Las Palmas. En ese mensaje demostró mucha madurez, porque no es fácil tomar esa decisión con esa edad". Mariola sabe que los focos se los está llevando Rafa, pero también es consciente de que Jorge forma parte del éxito de su hermano: "Jorge lo lleva muy bien. Muchos pensarán que puede tener envidia de su hermano, pero es todo lo contrario. Jorge está muy orgulloso de Rafa y lo toma con naturalidad. Están muy unidos. Lo primero que hizo Rafa cuando acabó el partido fue darle la camiseta a su hermano". Jorge juega en el Juvenil División de Honor amarillo, donde también destaca: "Se toma de muy buen humor que lo comparen con su hermano", sentencia Mariola. Dentro del equipo se ha encontrado con un hermano mayor, Álex Suárez: "Lo ha acogido como si fuera su padrino. Se porta muy bien con él y estamos encantados. Es un chico fantástico y le agradecemos cómo se porta con Rafa", explica Mariola. El capitán del equipo confirmó ante la prensa ese vínculo tan especial: "Lo tengo apadrinado y a mi lado siempre porque le tengo mucho cariño. Es humilde y está aprendiendo porque es un niño que está empezando. Hay que dejar que se equivoque y que disfrute. Será un gran futbolista". Algo en lo que coincide Alfonso: "Si se tiene paciencia con él, este chico no durará demasiado en Las Palmas. Estoy seguro que tocarán a su puerta los equipos grandes". Fran y Kevin Peréz son padre e hijo, y desde hace dos años se encargan de llevar la representación de los gemelos Cruz a través de la Agencia Élite FGC: "Ellos han sido fundamentales en todo lo que está sucediendo porque son mucho más que sus representantes. Han llegado en el momento que los chicos más lo necesitaban. Están muy atentos a los niños. Cuando Jorge se lesionó de la rótula, se involucraron en la recuperación desde el primer día. Ellos siempre hablan en plural porque, aunque Rafa sea el que haya debutado, confían y ayudan también mucho a su hermano Jorge", recalca Mariola.

articles.title: Enric Gallego, el delantero sin fecha de caducidad
articles.standfirst: A punto de cumplir 40 años, desafía al calendario con un arranque que lo sitúa como máximo goleador de Segunda
articles.summary: Enric Gallego, a punto de cumplir 40 años, desafía al calendario con un arranque que lo sitúa como máximo goleador de Segunda
articles.body: El DNI dice 39, pero el césped cuenta otra historia. Enric Gallego cumplirá 40 años en menos de 20 días y su olfato goleador se niega a envejecer. El delantero del Tenerife ha arrancado el curso como si el calendario no fuese con él. Corre. Presiona. Choca. Pelea. Y marca. Dos jornadas. Dos tantos. Seis puntos. Y el blanquiazul en lo más alto de la tabla de goleadores de Segunda.  Gallego vive uno de esos comienzos que desafían cualquier lógica futbolística. Mientras otros atacantes de su generación hace años que colgaron las botas, él sigue atacando el área adversaria con la voracidad de un veinteañero. No administra esfuerzos. No negocia duelos. No renuncia a una carrera. Su fútbol mantiene intacta una de las pocas virtudes que no entiende de edades: saber dónde va a caer la pelota. Es su gran secreto, pero no el único. Porque Gallego es un delantero de oficio. De los que entienden el juego. Sabe cuándo fijar a los centrales, cuándo caer a un costado y, sobre todo, cuándo aparecer en el lugar exacto para, como sucedió el pasado domingo en el Heliodoro, dar los tres puntos a los blanquiazules ante el Almería. "Estoy contento de aportar al equipo. Siempre trabajo, pero con goles todo va mejor. A ver si puedo seguir haciendo grande a Nacho Gil", bromeó elogiando al mediapunta que le ha empaquetado los dos goles que han terminado en la red del rival. La edad, lejos de ser un lastre, le ha dado más herramientas. El paso del tiempo no le ha quitado recursos a su juego. Más bien le ha añadido nuevas lecturas. "Este equipo sale a competir en cada jugada y cada duelo. Sabemos de dónde venimos y dónde queremos llegar. Tenemos que ir, aunque suene a tópico, semana a semana. No me marco cifras. Quiero seguir disfrutando con lo que hago. Los delanteros vivimos de rachas y quiero exprimir esta todo lo que pueda", explicó el capitán. Su carrera no responde al guion habitual de una estrella precoz. Llegó a Primera con 32 años y, justo donde muchos empiezan a escribir su epílogo deportivo, Gallego empezó a desgranar los capítulos más importantes. El Tenerife se ha convertido en uno de ellos. La isla es un escenario en el que su fútbol encaja y la grada lo venera. Nadie olvida sus 19 dianas en Primera RFEF para lograr el último ascenso. Como blanquiazul suma ya 57 goles y tiene a tiro los 63 que rubricó la leyenda Rommel Fernández. El gran ídolo del Heliodoro tampoco parece dispuesto a negociar con el calendario. Reivindica que no existe una edad exacta para dejar de competir al máximo nivel. Sobre todo, porque el mapa con todos los secretos del área sigue intacto en su cerebro. Así que, mientras sea feliz y acuda a su cita con la red, continuará siendo un delantero sin fecha de caducidad.

articles.title: Una obra de arte de Velázquez
articles.standfirst: Suyos fueron tres de los nueve goles del Madrid a la Real en 1967
articles.summary: Suyos fueron tres de los nueve goles del Madrid a la Real en 1967
articles.body: Bajaba Miguel Muñoz una tarde de pretemporada desde el hotel del Madrid en Navacerrada hacia el campo de entrenamiento. “Ahí está, tomando el sol”, comentó al divisar a uno de sus jugadores tumbado mientras apuraba los últimos rayos de la tarde. Era Manuel Velázquez. Muñoz le ordenó regresar al hotel: entendía que tomar el sol antes de empezar a correr era una señal de que no tenía demasiadas ganas de trabajar. La de Velázquez es una de esas historias reservadas a los genios a los que muchas veces no se entiende. Un número 10 de clase exquisita que en más de una ocasión provocó el enfado del Bernabéu por desaparecer de los partidos o por no dejarse la piel en balones imposibles. "Para eso ya estaba Pirri", solía decir De Felipe, gran amigo de Velázquez (1943-2016) y compañero suyo en el Real Madrid. Quienes más le trataron hablan de una persona de educación exquisita, de valores inquebrantables y capaz de plantarle cara al mismísimo Santiago Bernabéu si consideraba que la razón estaba de su parte. O de la de sus compañeros. Y quienes le vieron jugar recuerdan a un futbolista de una calidad extraordinaria, dueño de una visión de juego fuera de lo común. A él le colgaron, entre otras muchas etiquetas, la de ser el hombre que retiró a Puskas. Pero la realidad fue mucho más simple: no fue Velázquez quien retiró al húngaro, sino el fútbol y el paso de los años. Velázquez dejó muchas clases magistrales en los 402 partidos oficiales que jugó con el Madrid. El primero fue en plenas Navidades de 1965, el 26 de diciembre, en un 2-5 en Mallorca; el último, el 22 de mayo de 1977, contra el Málaga, en Chamartín (2-1). Cerebro de profesión, con el Madrid ganó seis Ligas, tres Copas y la Copa de Europa de 1966. Marcó 59 goles. Tres de ellos en un mismo partido: la goleada por 9-1 ante la Real Sociedad del 15 de septiembre de 1967. Era la segunda jornada de Liga. El Madrid se había estrenado con una victoria en campo del Sevilla (0-2) y la Real derrotando al Pontevedra en Atotxa. A pesar de su estreno victorioso, los vascos llegaron a Madrid repletos de temores. La noche antes del partido, Andoni Elizondo, entrenador de la Real, departía con MARCA en el hall del hotel Zurbano. Su mensaje mezclaba sensaciones: “Es muy posible que perdamos, pero no salimos derrotados. A un equipo que trabaja y lucha como la Real es muy difícil ganarle”. Ese mensaje quedó arrasado por lo que sucedió sobre el verde del Bernabéu en un partido que es la mayor derrota de la Real en la historia de la Liga. “De mala suerte, nada. Tal vez los primeros goles nos comieron la moral, motivando que descuidáramos demasiado el marcaje, así como el sistema defensivo. No creo que nos afecte, porque veníamos preparados para algo parecido”, aseguraba tras la paliza recibida Josemari Martínez, el capitán de un equipo en el que jugaba quien, como entrenador, le daría a la Real las dos Ligas que tiene: Alberto Ormaetxea. Gran parte de las explicaciones para entender el 9-1 de aquella noche madrileña de finales de verano estuvieron en el gran partido de Velázquez. Primero repartió juego desde su cátedra del 10; después marcó goles como en ningún otro partido de su carrera. Suyos fueron el quinto, el sexto y el séptimo del Madrid. “Han sido tres goles muy parecidos. Grosso y Amancio me han dado tres pases extraordinarios y, en todas las ocasiones, he tenido tiempo para avanzar y disparar antes de que saliera el portero. Creo que dos goles entraron por el mismo sitio; el otro, por el lado contrario. Pero los tres los marqué desde la misma demarcación”, contaba el goleador. No se llevó el balón a casa, porque a esa tradición británica aún le quedaban tres años para llegar a España de la mano del Athletic. La exhibición del Madrid y de Velázquez no la vio Bernabéu. Don Santiago vivía una época en la que su presencia en los partidos de casa era una excepción. Más allá del homenaje a Di Stéfano, ante el Celtic el 7 de junio de 1967, el presidente blanco era reacio a dejarse ver en Chamartín. Sí estuvo su mujer, doña María, quien explicó que Bernabéu había decidido esta vez quedarse en casa porque al día siguiente le esperaba un viaje a Ámsterdam. Al Madrid le aguardaba el Ajax y un chico del que empezaba a hablarse mucho: un tal Johan Cruyff.

articles.title: La sombra de Lunin
articles.standfirst: El meta ucraniano arranca su séptima temporada a la sombra de Courtois
articles.summary: El meta ucraniano arranca su séptima temporada a la sombra de Courtois
articles.body: Hay porteros que han hecho su carrera en la sombra, pasando más partidos en el banquillo que defendiendo la portería de su equipo. Entre todos ellos asombra la historia de Tommaso Berni. El italiano se pasó siete temporadas en el Inter, más otra anterior en el Torino, sin jugar un solo minuto. Lo que no evitó que fuera expulsado dos veces. En la España de los 80 se hizo popular la figura de Carlos Meléndez. Fue suplente eterno en Bilbao (de Iribar, Aguirreoa y Zubizarreta) y después en el Espanyol de N'Kono y Biurrun. Una figura que, sin jugar, hizo el viaje de San Mamés a Sarrià al lado de Javier Clemente. En este Real Madrid del regreso de Mourinho, Andriy Lunin arranca su séptima temporada a la sombra de Courtois. El belga ya forma parte de la historia de la portería blanca. Para muchos, el guardameta más grande de la historia del club, por encima de Casillas, Zamora, Araquistain... Un dominio de su puesto que no admite debate alguno y que apenas encuentra puntos débiles en su primera temporada en la Casa Blanca: en la 2018-19. El portero ucraniano, después de un par de años de cesiones, se instaló en la primera plantilla del Madrid en el verano de 2020, el de la pandemia. A esas alturas, Courtois ya era intocable para Zidane. Como luego lo fue para Ancelotti, Xabi Alonso, Arbeloa y, ahora, Mourinho. En ese recorrido de portero suplente de largo aliento apareció un oasis: la temporada 2023-24. La grave lesión de rodilla que sufrió Courtois a las puertas de LaLiga llevó al club a fichar a Kepa. Parecía una condena a otra suplencia para el ucraniano. Sin embargo, tras la Supercopa de España, Lunin se convirtió en el titular y en el héroe del Madrid en la tanda de penaltis del Etihad. Eso sí, en cuanto Courtois estuvo listo para regresar, Ancelotti volvió a darle las llaves de la portería. Suya fue la final de la Champions en Wembley. Lunin afronta la temporada con el mismo papel de las anteriores: a la sombra de Courtois y a la espera de que Mourinho le conceda oportunidades en la Copa. La temporada pasada apenas disputó el partido de Albacete hasta que las lesiones se cruzaron en el camino del guardameta belga y le abrieron las puertas de la titularidad. articles.title: Mourinho y sus dos teorías sobre Vinicius
articles.standfirst: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.summary: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.body: Ya sé que vais a decir que dije…” adelantó Mourinho antes de comentar los sucesos en torno a Vinicius, y luego dio paso a ello desgranando los clásicos y razonables argumentos de la defensa: le buscan, le golpean, siempre van a por él para sacarle del juego porque es muy bueno… Todo es verdad, como lo era lo que comentó después del partido de Lisboa: que provoca, que canta el gol de manera ofensiva, que siempre le pasa a él, que da lugar a que le ocurra lo que le ocurre… Son las dos caras de la misma moneda, dos formas perfectamente razonables de explicar la polémica que le acompaña. La visión del defensor y la del fiscal ante un mismo suceso. Según en qué lado estés, o te pille, lo puedes contar de una forma y otra. A él le tocó enfrente en Lisboa, del lado de Vinicius en Cornellà, y de ahí sus dos versiones, igualmente veraces y discutibles. Otra vez el problema del huevo y la gallina. ¿Quién empieza? Convengamos que, al menos en Cornellà, empezó Cala con su patadita al riñón. Lo malo para Vinicius es que la bola de nieve ya echó a rodar hace mucho, y que vaya donde vaya la diversión es excitarle. Mourinho tiene ante sí la tarea de sosegar sus reacciones, porque en lo del contrario no puede influir. Vinicius aparte, Mou ha regresado con ganas de explayarse largamente y en general bien en las conferencias de prensa, algo que agradecer. En Cornellà dejó buenas explicaciones estrictamente futbolísticas sobre cuestiones como, por ejemplo, la conveniencia de aproximar a Bellingham al gol o la posibilidad de hacer de Güler un jugador útil en el arranque del juego… Es bueno que los entrenadores hablen de fútbol, cosa que la mayoría sólo suelen hacer cuando les pillas en privado, o esa es mi experiencia, y rara vez cuando hablan ‘urbi et orbi’ como es el caso de las ruedas de prensa, cuando su ciencia y sus proyectos pueden tener mayor alcance, cayendo como lluvia provechosa para todos los aficionados. En general prefieren ser lacónicos, como si manejaran arcanos a proteger del conocimiento general. Ojalá cunda el ejemplo.

articles.title: La semana de fichajes que marcará todo
articles.standfirst: 'En Copa de Balón', una opinión de Elías Israel
articles.summary: 'En Copa de Balón', una opinión de Elías Israel
articles.body: Pregúntenle a cualquier entrenador de Primera cuál es la semana más importante de su temporada y ninguno les señalará un derbi. Les señalará ésta. La que empieza hoy. Porque un partido se pierde y se recupera, pero una plantilla mal cerrada no se recupera, se arrastra. No hay discurso, ni pizarra, ni sesión de vídeo que corrija a un vestuario corto. Los directores deportivos llevan todo el verano trabajando para esta semana, porque es cuando el mercado por fin se ablanda. No hay magia. Hay meses de llamadas para estar en el sitio exacto el día correcto. En el primer escalón pelean los juegan a otra cosa: El Barça sigue pendiente de su Plan A, que es tan sencillo de enunciar como difícil de resolver: un delantero titular. Uno que garantice los goles de Lewandowski y Ferran Torres. La exhibición de Elche puede ser impostora. Si se quiere pelear por la Champions, ésa figura es clave. El Madrid, en cambio, tiene plan B. Se llama Espí y le da una respuesta arriba. Su problema está en el medio. Necesita imperiosamente al centrocampista que le permita dominar el juego, ese Rodri que no llegó. En el segundo escalón, el Atlético dirime estos días su plan J. J de Julián. El desapego del Metropolitano con ‘La Araña’ ha dejado de ser una pitada memorable para convertirse en una decisión difícil. Julián está mustio, desorientado por sus agentes, y ese estado anímico invita a pensar en una gran venta a la Premier necesaria. En el tercer escalón, solo hay un objetivo: sobrevivir como se pueda. Monchi intenta hacer su magia de siempre con Bryan Zaragoza, que es su manera de recordar que el ingenio todavía cotiza. Toni Muñoz reinventa el Getafe a un coste irrisorio, un ejercicio que en cualquier otra Liga tendría nombre de escuela de negocios. Las penalidades reales de la competición se vieron con crudeza en el Osasuna-Levante: dos clubes que han ingresado una cantidad muy considerable por Víctor Muñoz y Carlos Espí, respectivamente, y que no reinvierten ni una quinta parte de lo cobrado. Eso también es la Liga. Valencia y Sevilla gestionan sus miserias dirigenciales de la mejor manera posible, que es un elogio triste. El Betis necesita acelerar, porque su mercado no va en absoluto acorde con las ilusiones que genera. Y la Real Sociedad lo ha dejado todo para el final, con todo lo que eso conlleva. Me salen hasta diez equipos que se agarran a lo que hay y solo sueñan con que haya tres equipos peores. Es un objetivo modesto, pero es el objetivo real de demasiados. La semana decisiva de otro mercado recesivo. Salvo para los grandes, que un año más juegan en otra Liga.

articles.title: Jose Mourinho 'calmer' as he enjoys Real Madrid return
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho claims to be a much cooler character as he prepares for his first home game in charge of Real Madrid since 2013 against Real Sociedad on Wednes...
articles.body:
Jose Mourinho claims to be a much cooler character as he prepares for his first home game in charge of Real Madrid since 2013 against Real Sociedad on Wednesday night.

But the 63-year-old conceded his relaxed demeanour might not last if his latest group of Galacticos fail to bridge the eight-point gap that saw them finish second in last season's LaLiga behind rivals Barcelona .

Mourinho began his latest spell in charge with a hard-fought 2-1 win over Espanyol at the weekend and believes he has seen enough to keep his notorious temper at bay for the time being.

"For years now I've felt calmer, with more control over my emotions," said Mourinho, whose first spell had its most controversial moment when he poked then-Barcelona coach Tito Vilanova in the eye after a Spanish Super Cup tie in 2011.

"But we will have to face difficult and frustrating situations that will come, which haven't come yet because we won the first match and I haven't seen anyone slacking off yet.

"I like that people work for Real Madrid, not just at Real Madrid. So far, I haven't felt any laziness, I've seen that everyone wants to give their best.

"Maybe it's the players and the people who work here who are protecting me from the darker side of my personality. But I feel good this way."

Mourinho was in a magnanimous mood after the opening game, praising his opponents and even the referee, and was at pains to play down the importance of his own personal reappearance on the touchline at the Bernabeu.

"I don't want the Bernabeu to welcome me in a particular way, I want it to welcome the team as its team and its passion," Mourinho added.

"I think people have already got a feeling for the way the team is working, its commitment, and the will to do things right. That's the most important thing - I'm not important.

"At the Bernabeu, we hope for the support of our people. What I expect is for the players to have the same hunger to win the match, the same attitude, resilience, strength and calmness to face a difficult game.

"I hope the fans can look at the team and recognise this kind of mentality, and maybe this kind of mentality can make the Bernabeu even stronger."

Aurelien Tchouameni has dropped out of the Real Madrid squad for the match, while Mourinho has indicated his desire to act sparingly with the likes of Jude Bellingham who returned for pre-season having undergone lengthy World Cup campaigns.

Sociedad, who opened their new campaign with a 1-0 defeat to Real Betis on Friday, have named Goncalo Guedes in their squad for the first time since he was forced to pull out of Portugal's World Cup squad due to injury.

articles.title: Olivia Smith: Â£1m Arsenal striker wins second straight PFA young player award
articles.summary: Olivia Smith's career has been in the limelight since she was 15 - but she had been preparing herself for it even before she was a professional footballer.
articles.body:
Olivia Smith has lived her life under a spotlight since she was 15 - but she had been preparing herself even before she became a professional footballer.

Now 22, Smith became the first Â£1m women's footballer last year when Arsenal signed her in a world record deal from Liverpool.

She had joined Liverpool for a club record of Â£210,000 just one season earlier, having made a name for herself when she was given her Canada debut aged 15.

Smith became the first woman to score for Liverpool at Anfield in a Women's Super League match in October 2025.

Now, for the second year in a row, she is the first non-English recipient of the PFA women's young player of the year award.

But how did Smith's sacrifices early in life help her reach the top?

Humble & sweet, but a lion - the story of the first female Â£1m player Published 6 September 2025

Humble & sweet, but a lion - the story of the first female Â£1m player

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

Splits, planks, South American and Jamaican flair

Smith grew up in the small Canadian city of Whitby, where from a young age she was encouraged to play football by her father, Sean.

She jumped between local clubs every year and played with boys until the age of 12 before finally settling into a girls' team.

Clearly talented, she continued to train with boys at the same time, while enjoying a multi-cultural upbringing around Toronto.

"My parents have made a lot of sacrifices taking me to all these places and moving every couple of years," Smith told BBC Sport.

"My dad's Jamaican, my mom's Chilean and Peruvian. There's so much football culture within those.

"I grasped a lot of that from my dad's dad who played football and my mom's dad also played in South America. I think I have that flair in my DNA.

"Of course, I [enjoy the different] food, music, all those kinds of things. In Toronto, you find it is a very multicultural place and that was really cool growing up."

But Smith later experienced bullying and turned to different sports as coping mechanisms, not knowing at the time how it would help her football career.

"I did taekwondo as a kid. I was getting bullied in school so it was more of a defensive mechanism kind of thing," said Smith.

"I did gymnastics too. That really helps with my agility. I find that, for my stature, I'm quite flexible as well, which really helps injury prevention.

"Taekwondo really helped with my discipline and arguably my shooting ability in terms of its speed.

"I think mainly it was just to keep me active, out of trouble, and it was just for fun. Thankfully it contributed to my footballing career."

Smith also thinks the unusual sporting background helped her when dealing with attention and pressure, as well as bullying.

"It helps with just the discipline on and off the pitch in simple tasks that are really important in my day-to-day life," added Smith.

"In gymnastics, you have to do splits or planks for [a length of time]. It's really hard mentally so that helped me mature. I developed a lot of mental toughness."

Dad's goals diary, Smith's Ballon d'Or dreams

It is not just Smith who has invested in football since a young age. Her dad, Sean, was tracking her statistics to monitor her progress.

"That is his favourite thing in the world to do. When I was younger, he would literally film all my games," said Smith.

"After games, we would go back and watch everything, see what I could have done better and what I did well.

"He kept a diary of the goals that I scored, what minute it was in and things like that. He still has it to this day. He loves it!"

Beyond football, Smith loves to cook and watch TV series - Law and Order: SVU is a current favourite - and she says she is "dying to get a puppy".

The young forward has learned to become independent, having left home as a teenager in order to chase a professional career.

But it hasn't been easy. When Smith moved to Michigan aged 15 on her own, she didn't know where she would be living when she boarded the plane.

"Moving around a lot, you're sacrificing relationships because you make good friends in one place, then you have to move," said Smith.

"That makes it quite tough, especially when you're young. I struggled a lot with that. I had to leave to get training elsewhere.

"It helped me get used to what was to come, so I think it was a very important sacrifice in my journey.

"I'm so grateful that I've been able to make so many connections in different places, so even though I'm away from home I feel like I have family."

For the first time in her career, Smith is about to begin a second season at the same club having settled into life at Arsenal.

"When I stepped into the building for my second pre-season it just felt surreal. It feels like home. It feels like Arsenal's the place that's meant to be," said Smith.

"It's an honour to be here. I'm just super excited to see where it takes me. I've always wanted to be somewhere for more than a year; I've moved around so much.

"I also knew there was so much more for me and I wanted to be the best that I could be. All those moves led me here."

At the age of six or seven, she wrote down in a journal what she wanted to achieve.

"I had a journal with everything in it that I wanted to accomplish and what I wanted to do: I want to win the Ballon d'Or. I want to win the World Cup," she added.

"That's still the case today. I want to win trophies with [Arsenal]. I've had this mentality since I was young. It is what has driven me this far."

articles.title: Joao Pedro: Is Brazilian ready to break Chelsea's so-called number nine curse?
articles.summary: Joao Pedro took just 31 seconds to score his opening goal of the season - will the new number nine reach the 20 he scored last season while wearing the number 20 shirt?
articles.body:
Joao Pedro took just 31 seconds to make a statement about how he is handling the so-called curse of the number nine shirt at Chelsea .

The Brazilian deftly lifted his shot over Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno to set his side on their way to a dramatic 3-2 win at Craven Cottage in manager Xabi Alonso's first game in charge on Monday.

It was a memorable weekend for Joao Pedro personally, having been handed the coveted number nine shirt and improved financial terms on a new contract that will run until 2034.

It might seem trite, but there is a sizeable group of Chelsea supporters who believe in the so-called curse.

Not since Dutch striker Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink left the club in 2004 have the club had a prolific striker in the number nine shirt.

Didier Drogba wore number 11 during his successful spell at Stamford Bridge and Diego Costa had the number 19 shirt, but high-profile forwards including Romelu Lukaku, Alvaro Morata, Gonzalo Higuain, Radamel Falcao and Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang struggled while wearing number nine.

All endured difficult and relatively short periods at the club.

The last player to wear the shirt before Joao Pedro was Liam Delap, who is currently in talks with Nottingham Forest about leaving Stamford Bridge after scoring only one Premier League goal last season.

Non-strikers, including midfielder Steve Sidwell and defender Khalid Boulahrouz, also wore the shirt, although some supporters would argue Tammy Abraham performed well as the number nine before his move to Roma.

Asked about the curse after scoring against Fulham , while starring alongside both Cole Palmer and club-record Â£117m signing Morgan Rogers, Joao Pedro told the Mirror: "I don't believe in that. I don't think numbers can decide this pressure."

Last season, the 24-year-old matched his shirt number by scoring 20 goals in all competitions, becoming the first Chelsea striker since Diego Costa to reach that mark nine years earlier.

It has left the Blues delighted with the Â£55m deal, plus up to Â£5m in add-ons, they agreed with Brighton to sign the forward last summer. Those close to Joao Pedro also believe his recent recognition is justified.

In addition, his close-knit entourage have no concerns about his ability to handle the pressure of being Chelsea 's leading man, having shared in his remarkable rise to the top.

Three reasons Chelsea could challenge for title - and one they may not Published 1 day ago

Three reasons Chelsea could challenge for title - and one they may not

Building resilience & physical strength after struggles

"If I gave him one thing, it is to fight for what you want all the time," his mother Flavia Junqueira explained to BBC Sport.

Looking at Joao Pedro's story, that is exactly what he has had to do.

His mother, along with his grandmother, have largely brought him up.

Reports from Joao Pedro's early childhood show his father, former Botafogo footballer Jose Joao de Jesus - more commonly known as Chicao - spent around eight years in prison after being charged as an accessory to murder and was rarely around.

Junqueira later separated from him and focused on her son's footballing potential.

"Joao had a dream," she said. "I shared that dream with my son. The dream didn't have a price."

Growing up in Ribeirao Preto, a nine-hour drive inland from Rio de Janeiro, Joao Pedro was eventually scouted by one of the city's clubs Fluminense, along with a host of other leading Brazilian clubs.

Fluminense were regarded as the best option for the youngster's development, who, like his father, began as a defensive midfielder before progressing further forward.

That choice was, however, fraught with difficulty.

Junqueira left her job, friends and family for Rio, and Joao Pedro "cried a lot" during the journey and in the weeks that followed because of homesickness.

Even in the academy, he was told he "wasn't strong enough" and would not make it. Again, it made him cry.

But his mother, despite her increasingly limited means after leaving her job, hired a personal trainer for her son.

At first, he ate well and trained well only because she told him to. Eventually, however, the penny dropped.

"He was very skinny and there was a significant physical disparity between him and the other athletes in his age group," his long-time personal trainer Rodrigo Goncalves told BBC Sport.

"He never stopped training. Sometimes he went a bit reluctantly, pushed by his mother, but he went.

"Over the years, however, that changed. He began to mature and understand that training wasn't just something his mother required, but rather a tool to improve his performance, develop his body and build the physical balance needed for football."

Joao Pedro became one of the stars of Fluminense's academy and was spotted by Watford's South America scout Rafa Monfort. A phone call from now- Tottenham striker Richarlison, who had made the same move, also proved crucial.

As a child, Joao Pedro was hooked on Premier League football, so the idea of moving to Watford appealed to him. However, it took around eight months to meet the Governing Body Endorsement criteria and secure a UK work permit.

Junqueira believes an overhead kick scored by Joao Pedro, then 17, against Cruzeiro in May 2019 helped convince decision-makers he was an exceptional talent worthy of the move.

When the family arrived in December 2019, Junqueira had not anticipated her bank cards would not work in England. However, then-Watford goalkeeper Heurelho Gomes, also Brazilian, took them under his wing and even bought them Christmas dinner.

A few months later, Covid and lockdown arrived, but Joao Pedro used the unprecedented period to focus on physical training with Goncalves again. He transformed his body by gaining around eight kilograms of body mass and became Premier League-ready.

After that period, he was no longer the little boy who cried, but a fully-fledged top-flight star capable of taking each step and challenge in his stride.

Joao Pedro extends Chelsea stay until 2034 Published 3 days ago

Joao Pedro extends Chelsea stay until 2034

Delap loses number nine shirt & trains away from first team Published 6 days ago

Delap loses number nine shirt & trains away from first team

'When he's angry, he doesn't shout, but goes quiet'

After a deal was agreed with Brighton last summer, Joao Pedro left a training camp in Rio de Janeiro under the guidance of Goncalves to join the Chelsea squad in Miami and immediately take part in the Fifa Club World Cup.

Remarkably, he scored twice in the semi-final against former club Fluminense - just days after arriving at the club. He was also on target in a sensational 3-0 win over Paris St-Germain in the final, widely regarded as Chelsea 's best moment under their current American ownership.

The Blues endured a dismal campaign following that triumph, finishing 10th in the Premier League and ending the season without a trophy and failing to qualify for Europe.

Despite that, Joao Pedro won Chelsea 's player of the season award and is among a group of senior players convinced the project can succeed under Alonso.

Like midfielder Moises Caicedo and captain Reece James, he signed a new contract, while Palmer has also outlined his commitment to stay amid links with Manchester United .

All four are viewed as key culture-setters at the club.

Joao Pedro, in particular, impressed staff by giving more interviews than any other player during a season in which there were few positives to discuss.

Multiple sources have previously told BBC Sport Chelsea have a dressing-room culture problem, specifically with cliques forming along language lines.

Joao Pedro and Palmer, who count each other among their closest friends, are viewed as two of the players capable of naturally bridging those divides.

It helps that Joao Pedro has his family in the UK and has embraced aspects of local culture, having first developed an interest through his love of the Premier League. He is known to listen to trap music, a UK form of hip-hop, and both he and Palmer appeared in pop icon Madonna's promotional short film Confessions II in June.

One of Alonso's main objectives is to rebuild a wayward culture which some sources have described to BBC Sport as overly "transactional" and "cold".

After his front three, including debutant Rogers, scored against Fulham , Alonso said: "They need to take responsibility. They need to lead the rest. They need to inspire the rest because if they do great, the others will follow."

Few know how Joao Pedro handled his omission from the Brazil squad at the World Cup, where they were knocked out in the last 16 by Norway this summer.

Even those closest to him do not know how disappointed he was to miss out, given that playing for Brazil at a World Cup had long been one of his biggest dreams.

"When Joao Pedro is angry, he doesn't shout, he goes quiet," Junqueira said of his general personality.

After Chelsea 's struggles season and the lack of World Cup involvement, he had two weeks completely off.

Joao Pedro spent the rest of his summer in Rio training with Goncalves, his personal fitness coach since childhood, surrounded by friends and following many of the same routines he always has.
